02 / Projects

Research

  • Ethnography · Peru

    Mantaro Valley

    My doctoral research examines Wanka identity through two practices in Peru’s Mantaro Valley: gourd carving in Cochas Chico and the pagapu offering ritual at Huaytapallana.

  • Material culture · Provenance

    Between the Andes and the Alps

    I trace the journey of a gourd carved by Guillermo Ventura. Johanna Schupp bought it in Cochas Chico in 1983, brought it to Borken in 1987, and donated it to the BASA Museum in 2021. Cataloged as Schu18, the gourd depicts a child’s illness, diagnosis, and recovery in 31 scenes set in the Mantaro Valley.

    Talk program at the Museum der Kulturen Basel ↗
    Presentation at the Folger Salon ↗

  • Online exhibition · BASA Museum · 2026

    Landscapes in Transformation. The Cochabamba Valley Beyond the Inkas

    I created the online exhibition in ArcGIS StoryMaps and translated all exhibition texts into German and English. The exhibition brings together objects from the Bonn Collection of the Americas, colonial sources, and local memories to show how different societies have shaped the Cochabamba Valley.

    Take the virtual tour in ArcGIS StoryMaps ↗
    Exhibition website on GitHub Pages ↗
    Read the exhibition symposium in Amerigrafías ↗
    About the exhibition at the University of Bonn ↗

  • Exhibition · BASA Museum · 2025–2026

    Mehr als nur Buchstaben

    The exhibition brought together objects that convey stories and knowledge through images and signs across the Americas. For the catalog, I wrote the entry on Guillermo Ventura’s carved gourd and a text on the Wanka.

    View the exhibition in the BASA Museum archive ↗

  • Exhibition · P26 · 2024–2025

    Auf Spurensuche

    I contributed to the BASA Museum’s presentation in this University of Bonn exhibition on the provenance of objects. Guillermo Ventura’s carved gourd Schu18 was among the objects on display.

    View the P26 exhibition at the University of Bonn ↗

03 / Writing

Publications

  • 2025 · Co-authored interview

    Making the Ancestors Speak

    A conversation with Kerstin Nowack about Udo Oberem, Catherine Julien, and the use of sources in Andean ethnohistory.

    Read in Notas de Antropología de las Américas ↗

  • 2025 · Co-authored article

    Illness, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Cure: Carving Sorcery in the Mantaro Valley

    The article traces the provenance of Schu18 and examines how its carved scenes depict chacho illness and jubeo de cuy, a diagnostic practice involving a guinea pig.

    Read in Bulletin of Hispanic Studies ↗

  • 2024 · Audio review

    The “Koppers Feuerland” Wax Cylinders

    A review of the digitization of phonograph cylinder recordings from Tierra del Fuego.

    Read on bonndoc ↗
